title: Adaptive Compatibility Proxy: Negotiated Mapping for Streaming, Toolcall & Structured Output
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Spike + implementation work to build an adaptive compatibility proxy that negotiates feature mappings between OpenAI Responses-style clients and Redwood's runtime. Focus areas: streaming event model differences, function/tool-call semantics, structured-output schema fidelity, and lossiness detection. Goal is a negotiated per-session translation layer that minimizes behavioral drift while preserving latency SLOs and token provenance.
technical_design: We propose a lightweight adaptive proxy that performs a capability negotiation handshake at session start. The handshake records client expectations (streaming chunking, function-call vs tool-call framing, structured-output schema preferences, max tolerated added latency). Based on capabilities, the proxy chooses one of three mapping strategies: 1) Passthrough (no translation), 2) Lossless adapter (reformats events but preserves original token/offset provenance), 3) Best-effort shim (when features are incompatible, apply heuristics with clear provenance flags). The proxy includes: - streaming boundary mapper (coalesces/splits events to match client framing while keeping token offsets) - toolcall orchestrator (ensures at-most-once execution semantics via idempotency tokens and execution receipts) - structured-output enforcer (schema validator and repair heuristics with guarded rewrites) - telemetry hooks (trace parent, token provenance header, fidelity_score). Decisions trade off extra latency vs. fidelity; choose conservatively by default with an opt-in low-latency mode.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Contract tests covering 95% of OpenAI Responses event shapes pass under the Lossless adapter mode. 2) Median added latency for small requests <= 20ms; p95 <= 75ms under standard load. 3) No regressions in tool-call atomicity: tool backend logs show idempotent delivery with <0.1% duplicates in canary. 4) Structured-output roundtrip fidelity >= 99% for target JSON schemas on synthetic corpus. 5) Telemetry surface shows token provenance header on all proxied responses. 6) Feature-flagged rollout completed with canary passing for three customers and no elevated error budget usage for 24h.
testing_plan: Unit tests for the negotiation state machine and mapping transforms. Integration tests with mock OpenAI Responses client that exercises: chunked streaming, interleaved toolcall+stream, function-call nesting, and malformed structured outputs. Fuzz tests to detect event-boundary misalignments. Performance bench harness with representative payloads to measure added latency and memory. End-to-end canary using two internal sandbox customers, with scripted call patterns and automated contract verification. Run chaos test to simulate dropped events and delayed kernel responses.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag (runtime.capability_proxy=false). 2) Internal QA run and load test. 3) Enable for 1% of traffic for dedicated customers (canary group A) for 48h. 4) Expand to 10% if no regressions for 72h. 5) Add broader Hosted customers (by account opt-in) and evaluate. 6) Full rollout conditional on meeting acceptance criteria and security signoff. 7) Automatic rollback trigger on error-rate spike > 2x baseline or p95 latency jump > 2x baseline. Detailed rollout checklist in linked doc.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: Stream-splitting can lead to out-of-order semantics and double-tool-exec. Mitigation: idempotency tokens, sequence numbers, and server-side tool execution receipts; conservative default mapping. - Risk: Guarded schema rewrites may mask upstream model regressions. Mitigation: emit explicit provenance flags and include 'repair_score' in telemetry; route low-confidence repairs to canary only. - Risk: Added latency harms low-latency SLAs. Mitigation: fast-path passthrough for clients that accept our native shapes; perf optimizations (zero-copy buffering, async write batching). - Risk: Security/privilege escalation via tool-call retries. Mitigation: enforce RBAC at proxy, require signed execution receipts for replay acceptance.
